symbols.name: \(\ell\)
symbols.def: Index along which the pre-period and post-period cell sample sizes diverge.

symbols.name: \(J\)
symbols.def: Number of donor units, fixed as \(\ell\) varies.

symbols.name: \(T_0\)
symbols.def: Number of pre-intervention periods.

symbols.name: \(T_1\)
symbols.def: Number of post-intervention periods.

symbols.name: \(j\)
symbols.def: The value \(j=0\) denotes the treated unit and \(j\geq 1\) denotes a donor.

symbols.name: \(t\)
symbols.def: Generic panel period.

symbols.name: \(r\)
symbols.def: Generic atom index in a finite-support post-period cell.

symbols.name: \(u\)
symbols.def: Generic argument of a quantile function.

symbols.name: \(q\)
symbols.def: Generic index for a signed coefficient--endpoint pair.

symbols.name: \(n_\ell\)
symbols.def: Number of independent observations in each pre-period unit--period cell at array index \(\ell\).

symbols.name: \(m_\ell\)
symbols.def: Number of independent observations in each post-period unit--period cell at array index \(\ell\).

symbols.name: \(S\)
symbols.def: Fixed upper bound on the number of atoms in every observed post-period cell.

symbols.name: \(D\)
symbols.def: Length of a common compact interval containing every outcome support.

symbols.name: \(f_{\min}\)
symbols.def: Uniform positive lower bound for pre-period cell densities.

symbols.name: \(f_{\max}\)
symbols.def: Uniform upper bound for pre-period cell densities.

symbols.name: \(L_f\)
symbols.def: Uniform bound on the absolute derivative of each pre-period density, with one-sided derivatives at endpoints.

symbols.name: \(\lambda\)
symbols.def: Uniform lower eigenvalue bound for the pooled donor Gram on the sum-zero subspace.

symbols.name: \(\pi_t\)
symbols.def: Fixed weights satisfying \(\sum_{t\leq T_0}\pi_t=1\).

symbols.name: \(\alpha\)
symbols.def: Nominal error probability for the simultaneous confidence ball.

symbols.name: \(\Delta_J\)
symbols.def: \(\Delta_J=\{v\in\mathbb R^J:v_j\geq0,\ \mathbf 1^\top v=1\}\).

symbols.name: \(L\)
symbols.def: \(L=\{v\in\mathbb R^J:\mathbf 1^\top v=0\}\).

symbols.name: \(F_{jt,\ell}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on a compact interval of length \(D\)
symbols.def: Outcome law of donor \(j\geq1\) in period \(t\) at array index \(\ell\).

symbols.name: \(F^N_{0t,\ell}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on a compact interval of length \(D\)
symbols.def: Potential outcome law of the treated unit without intervention.

symbols.name: \(F^I_{0t,\ell}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on a compact interval of length \(D\)
symbols.def: Observed treated outcome law in a post-intervention period.

symbols.name: \(Q_{jt,\ell}\)
symbols.def: Left-continuous generalized inverse of \(F_{jt,\ell}\).

symbols.name: \(Q^N_{0t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: Left-continuous generalized inverse of \(F^N_{0t,\ell}\).

symbols.name: \(Q^I_{0t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: Left-continuous generalized inverse of \(F^I_{0t,\ell}\).

symbols.name: \(w_\ell\)
symbols.def: Unique simplex weight that represents \(Q^N_{0t,\ell}\) from donor quantiles for every \(t\in\{1,\ldots,T_0\}\cup\{T_0+1,\ldots,T_0+T_1\}\); the second index set refers to the post-treatment no-intervention counterfactual law.

symbols.name: \(\widehat Q_{jt,\ell}\)
symbols.def: Empirical quantile function from the corresponding donor cell sample.

symbols.name: \(\widehat Q^N_{0t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: Empirical quantile function for the treated unit in a pre-period.

symbols.name: \(\widehat Q^I_{0t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: Empirical quantile function for the treated unit in a post-period.

symbols.name: \(\widehat w_\ell\)
symbols.def: Minimizer of the pooled empirical pre-period squared quantile loss.

symbols.name: \(\tau_{t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(\tau_{t,\ell}=Q^I_{0t,\ell}-Q^N_{0t,\ell}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\tau_{t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat\tau_{t,\ell}=\widehat Q^I_{0t,\ell}-\sum_{j=1}^J\widehat w_{\ell j}\widehat Q_{jt,\ell}\).

symbols.name: \(E_{t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(E_{t,\ell}=\|\widehat\tau_{t,\ell}-\tau_{t,\ell}\|_{L^2}^2\).

symbols.name: \(x_{jtr,\ell}\)
symbols.def: The \(r\)-th ordered support point of a post-period cell; the treated observed cell uses \(j=0\).

symbols.name: \(p_{jtr,\ell}\)
symbols.def: Probability mass at \(x_{jtr,\ell}\), retaining zero masses when convenient.

symbols.name: \(c_{jtr,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(c_{jtr,\ell}=\sum_{s\leq r}p_{jts,\ell}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat c_{jtr,\ell}\)
symbols.def: Empirical counterpart of \(c_{jtr,\ell}\) computed from the post-period cell sample.

symbols.name: \(\Delta_{jtr,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(\Delta_{jtr,\ell}=x_{jt(r+1),\ell}-x_{jtr,\ell}\).

symbols.name: \(b_{tq,\ell}\)
symbols.def: For each treated jump use coefficient \(-\Delta_{0tr,\ell}\), for each donor jump use \(w_{\ell j}\Delta_{jtr,\ell}\), and duplicate it with opposite sign at its population endpoint.

symbols.name: \(s_{tq,\ell}\)
symbols.def: Endpoint paired with \(b_{tq,\ell}\), equal to the corresponding empirical or population cumulative-mass knot.

symbols.name: \(Z_{jtr}\)
symbols.def: Gaussian limit of \(\sqrt{m_\ell}(\widehat c_{jtr,\ell}-c_{jtr,\ell})\), with Brownian-bridge covariance within a cell and independence across cells.

symbols.name: \(d_{jtr}\)
symbols.def: Finite within-cluster limit of the centered coordinate \(\sqrt{m_\ell}c_{jtr,\ell}\), after removing a cluster translation.

symbols.name: \(\Psi_t(d,Z)\)
symbols.def: \(\Psi_t(d,Z)=-\tfrac12\sum_{q,q'}b_{tq}b_{tq'}|s_{tq}(d,Z)-s_{tq'}(d,Z)|\), summed over local knot clusters with every population endpoint retained as its own anchor.

symbols.name: \(H_\ell\)
symbols.def: \(H_\ell=\sum_{t=1}^{T_0}\pi_t\int_0^1(Q_{1t,\ell}(u),\ldots,Q_{Jt,\ell}(u))^\top(Q_{1t,\ell}(u),\ldots,Q_{Jt,\ell}(u))du\).

symbols.name: \(H\)
symbols.def: \(H=\lim_{\ell\to\infty}H_\ell\) along a selected local subsequence on which the finite-array Grams converge.

symbols.name: \(q_t\)
symbols.def: \(q_t=(Q_{1t},\ldots,Q_{Jt})^\top\) along the local subsequence.

symbols.name: \(g\)
symbols.def: Limit of the centered pooled empirical pre-period quantile score on \(L\).

symbols.name: \(h\)
symbols.def: Coordinatewise limit of \(\sqrt{n_\ell}w_\ell\); an infinite coordinate removes the corresponding local inequality.

symbols.name: \(D_h\)
symbols.def: \(D_h=\{v\in L:v_j\geq-h_j\text{ for every finite }h_j\}\).

symbols.name: \(V_h\)
symbols.def: \(V_h=\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in D_h}\{v^\top Hv-2v^\top g\}\).

symbols.name: \(M_t\)
symbols.def: \(M_t=\int_0^1q_t(u)q_t(u)^\top du\) for the limiting post-period donor-quantile vector.

symbols.name: \(A_t(V_h)\)
symbols.def: \(A_t(V_h)=V_h^\top M_tV_h\).

symbols.name: \(\rho_\ell\)
symbols.def: \(\rho_\ell=n_\ell/\sqrt{m_\ell}\).

symbols.name: \(\kappa\)
symbols.def: A finite positive limit of \(\rho_\ell\).

symbols.name: \(\omega\)
symbols.def: \(\omega=\lim_{\ell\to\infty}n_\ell/(n_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell})\) along a convergent subsequence.

symbols.name: \(\eta\)
symbols.type: known coordinate of the local experiment
symbols.space: finite-dimensional design and within-cell offset data
symbols.def: Collection of limiting Gram and covariance objects, jump coefficients, the macro-cluster partition, the phase weight \(\omega\), and within-cell offset differences that are exactly observed in the local Gaussian experiment.

symbols.name: \(\Gamma_\eta\)
symbols.def: Feasible cross-cell knot translations and simplex-face offsets remaining after conditioning on \(\eta\), modulo irrelevant common translations.

symbols.name: \(\theta\)
symbols.def: A generic cross-cell translation and simplex-face offset compatible with the conditioned experiment.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal L_{\eta,\theta}\)
symbols.def: For \(\theta\in\Gamma_\eta\), \(\mathcal L_{\eta,\theta}=\max_{t>T_0}\{(1-\omega)A_t(V_h)+\omega\Psi_t(d,Z)\}\), where \(\omega=\lim n_\ell/(n_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell})\).

symbols.name: \(c_B^*\)
symbols.def: The least common 95 percent cutoff over the one-donor Bernoulli local-knot experiment, derived in \(\mathrm{thm:bernoulli-honesty-penalty}\).

symbols.name: \(P\)
symbols.def: A generic maintained data-generating law.

symbols.name: \(\varepsilon\)
symbols.def: Requested deterministic half-width of a certified cutoff bracket.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal M\)
symbols.def: The class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:model-class}\).

symbols.name: \(R_\ell\)
symbols.def: Generic measurable radius for the simultaneous product ball.

symbols.name: \(\varepsilon_{n,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(\varepsilon_{n,\ell}=\sqrt{\log(4(J+1)T_0/\alpha)/(2n_\ell)}\).

symbols.name: \(\varepsilon_{m,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(\varepsilon_{m,\ell}=\sqrt{\log(4(J+1)T_1/\alpha)/(2m_\ell)}\).

symbols.name: \(R_{w,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(R_{w,\ell}=\min\{\sqrt2,4\varepsilon_{n,\ell}/[f_{\min}(\sqrt\lambda-\sqrt J\varepsilon_{n,\ell}/f_{\min})]\}\) when the denominator is positive and \(\sqrt2\) otherwise.

symbols.name: \(R^{\mathrm{DKW}}_\ell\)
symbols.def: Radius constructed in \(\mathrm{def:dkw-fallback}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal C_\ell(R_\ell)\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_\ell(R_\ell)=\{(f_t)_{t>T_0}:\max_{t>T_0}\|f_t-\widehat\tau_{t,\ell}\|_{L^2}\leq R_\ell\}\).

symbols.name: \(q_{t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(q_{t,\ell}=(Q_{1t,\ell},\ldots,Q_{Jt,\ell})^\top\).

symbols.name: \(M_{t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(M_{t,\ell}=\int_0^1q_{t,\ell}(u)q_{t,\ell}(u)^\top du\).

symbols.name: \(A_{t,\ell}(v)\)
symbols.def: \(A_{t,\ell}(v)=v^\top M_{t,\ell}v\) for \(v\in L\).

symbols.name: \(\zeta_{jtr,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(\zeta_{jtr,\ell}=\sqrt{m_\ell}(\widehat c_{jtr,\ell}-c_{jtr,\ell})\).

symbols.name: \(\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}=-\tfrac12\sum_{q,q'}b_{tq,\ell}b_{tq',\ell}|\sqrt{m_\ell}s_{tq,\ell}-\sqrt{m_\ell}s_{tq',\ell}|\), where every jump contributes the two distinct pairs \((a,\widehat c)\) and \((-a,c)\).

symbols.name: \(\mathscr S_\eta\)
symbols.space: sub-sigma-fields of the finite Gaussian experiment
symbols.def: \(\mathscr S_\eta=\sigma(\eta)\), generated by the limiting design, jump coefficients, covariance and macro-cluster labels, together with all exactly observed within-cell offset differences.

symbols.name: \(\Sigma_\eta\)
symbols.def: Conditional covariance of the joint pre-score and post bridge coordinates given \(\mathscr S_\eta\), block diagonal between the independent pre and post samples and retaining within-cell bridge covariance.

symbols.name: \(\mathsf X_{\eta,\theta}\)
symbols.def: Given \(\mathscr S_\eta\), draw \((g,Z)\sim N(0,\Sigma_\eta)\); observe the pre coordinate \(h+H_L^{-1}g\) in any fixed coordinates on \(L\) and, for every shared-noise knot group, the coordinates \(d_i+Z_g\), where \(d_i-d_k\) within a cell is fixed by \(\eta\) and \(\theta\) supplies only the unresolved group translations and finite face offsets.

symbols.name: \(\Pr_{\eta,\theta}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the observation space
symbols.def: The law of \(\mathsf X_{\eta,\theta}\) conditional on \(\mathscr S_\eta\).

symbols.name: \(G\)
symbols.def: A deterministic bound for \(\|g\|_2\) on a certified Gaussian tail box.

symbols.name: \(R\)
symbols.def: A deterministic bound for the maximum absolute post bridge coordinate on a certified Gaussian tail box.

symbols.name: \(K_\eta\)
symbols.def: Maximum span of the within-cell offset differences recorded in \(\eta\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal B_{G,R}\)
symbols.space: compact subsets of the Gaussian-noise space
symbols.def: \(\mathcal B_{G,R}=\{(g,Z):\|g\|_2\leq G,\ \max_{j,t,r}|Z_{jtr}|\leq R\}\).

symbols.name: \(\Gamma_\eta^{G,R}\)
symbols.def: The union over finitely many endpoint orders and simplex active sets obtained on \(\mathcal B_{G,R}\) by capping every finite face offset at \(2G/\lambda\) and every successive shared-noise-group translation gap at \(2R+2K_\eta\), modulo a common translation.

symbols.name: \(\mathscr C_\eta\)
symbols.def: \(\mathscr C_\eta=\{c(\eta)\geq0:c\text{ is }\mathscr S_\eta\text{-measurable}\}\); after conditioning on \(\eta\), each member is one common deterministic cutoff for every \(\theta\in\Gamma_\eta\).

symbols.name: \(h_f\)
symbols.def: Local offset of the second donor weight in the certified \(J=2\), \(S=2\) instance.

symbols.name: \(h_c\)
symbols.def: Local displacement between the treated and first-donor Bernoulli cumulative-mass knots in the certified \(J=2\), \(S=2\) instance.

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak E_{2,2}(h_f,h_c)\)
symbols.def: The experiment constructed in \(\mathrm{def:j2s2-instance}\).

symbols.name: \(c^*(\eta,\alpha)\)
symbols.def: \(c^*(\eta,\alpha)=\inf\{c(\eta)\in\mathscr C_\eta:\inf_{\theta\in\Gamma_\eta}\Pr_{\eta,\theta}(\mathcal L_{\eta,\theta}\leq c(\eta))\geq1-\alpha\}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathsf{Handle}_{\mathrm{cert}}\)
symbols.def: A support-cluster and simplex-face procedure starting from simultaneous empirical-CDF, multinomial, pre-quantile, Gram, and covariance confidence regions; it conditions on estimable within-cell offset differences, maximizes certified Gaussian loss probabilities over unresolved cross-cell translations and face offsets in \(\Gamma_\eta^{G,R}\), and uses a rate-preserving DKW fallback under a deterministic work budget.

symbols.name: \(D^{\mathrm{post}}_{t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(D^{\mathrm{post}}_{t,\ell}=(\widehat Q^I_{0t,\ell}-Q^I_{0t,\ell})-\sum_{j=1}^Jw_{\ell j}(\widehat Q_{jt,\ell}-Q_{jt,\ell})\).

symbols.name: \(D_{t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(D_{t,\ell}=D^{\mathrm{post}}_{t,\ell}\).
symbols.role: finite-array post error alias used in the exact decomposition

symbols.name: \(v_\ell\)
symbols.def: \(v_\ell=\sqrt{n_\ell}(\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell)\).

symbols.name: \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}=(\widehat Q_{1t,\ell}-Q_{1t,\ell},\ldots,\widehat Q_{Jt,\ell}-Q_{Jt,\ell})^\top\).

symbols.name: \(B_{t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(B_{t,\ell}=\sqrt{m_\ell}\int_0^1q_{t,\ell}(u)D_{t,\ell}(u)du\).

symbols.name: \(B_t(d,Z)\)
symbols.def: Joint local-subsequence weak limit of \(B_{t,\ell}\), obtained by integrating the limiting donor quantiles against the separately anchored finite-support pulse process indexed by \(d\) and \(Z\).

symbols.name: \(r_{t,\ell}\)
symbols.def: \(r_{t,\ell}=-2(n_\ell m_\ell)^{-1/2}v_\ell^\top B_{t,\ell}+n_\ell^{-1}\|v_\ell^\top\epsilon_{t,\ell}\|_{L^2}^2-2n_\ell^{-1/2}\langle D_{t,\ell},v_\ell^\top\epsilon_{t,\ell}\rangle+2n_\ell^{-1}\langle v_\ell^\top q_{t,\ell},v_\ell^\top\epsilon_{t,\ell}\rangle\).

symbols.name: \(h_B\)
symbols.def: Local cumulative-mass-knot displacement in the one-donor Bernoulli honesty subexperiment.

symbols.name: \(\Psi^B_{h_B}\)
symbols.def: Specialization of \(\Psi_t(d,Z)\) to an equal-Bernoulli treated--donor pair with local knot displacement \(h_B\).

assumptions.condition: The counts \(J\), \(T_0\), \(T_1\), and \(S\) do not vary with \(\ell\).
Observations are independent and identically distributed within each unit--period cell and samples are independent across distinct cells and across the pre-period and post-period blocks.

For every \(\ell\) and every \(t\in\{1,\ldots,T_0\}\cup\{T_0+1,\ldots,T_0+T_1\}\), \(Q^N_{0t,\ell}=\sum_{j=1}^Jw_{\ell j}Q_{jt,\ell}\) almost everywhere on \([0,1]\), with the same \(w_\ell\) in all periods; for \(t>T_0\), \(Q^N_{0t,\ell}\) is the treated unit's counterfactual no-intervention quantile law, not the observed intervention law \(Q^I_{0t,\ell}\).

Every pre-period cell law has a continuously differentiable density on its compact support, bounded below by \(f_{\min}\), bounded above by \(f_{\max}\), and with absolute derivative bounded by \(L_f\), including the corresponding one-sided endpoint bounds.
For every \(\ell\) and every \(v\in L\), the finite-array pooled population Gram satisfies \(v^\top H_\ell v\geq\lambda\|v\|_2^2\).

standard.name: Uniform local quadratic identification on a boundary parameter space

assumptions.condition: Every observed post-period treated or donor law has at most \(S\) atoms in the common compact outcome interval of length \(D\).

definitions.name: Fixed-dimensional discrete-post DSC triangular-array class \(\mathcal M\)
Exact finite-array separately anchored endpoint energy
definitions.construction: For each post-period jump set \(a_{0tr,\ell}=-\Delta_{0tr,\ell}\) for the treated cell and \(a_{jtr,\ell}=w_{\ell j}\Delta_{jtr,\ell}\) for donor \(j\geq1\); retain both pairs \((a_{jtr,\ell},\widehat c_{jtr,\ell})\) and \((-a_{jtr,\ell},c_{jtr,\ell})\) as separate entries \((b_{tq,\ell},s_{tq,\ell})\), and set \(\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}=-\tfrac12\sum_{q,q'}b_{tq,\ell}b_{tq',\ell}|\sqrt{m_\ell}s_{tq,\ell}-\sqrt{m_\ell}s_{tq',\ell}|\).

definitions.name: Local-subsequence separately anchored endpoint energy
definitions.construction: For each finite root-\(m_\ell\) knot cluster, translate one anchor to zero, retain the known within-cell differences and the unresolved cross-cell translations, replace each empirical knot by \(d_{jtr}+Z_{jtr}\), retain the population anchor at \(d_{jtr}\), and set \(\Psi_t(d,Z)=-\tfrac12\sum_{q,q'}b_{tq}b_{tq'}|s_{tq}(d,Z)-s_{tq'}(d,Z)|\), summing over clusters.

definitions.name: Finite-array post-period weight quadratic
definitions.construction: Set \(q_{t,\ell}=(Q_{1t,\ell},\ldots,Q_{Jt,\ell})^\top\), \(M_{t,\ell}=\int_0^1q_{t,\ell}(u)q_{t,\ell}(u)^\top du\), and \(A_{t,\ell}(v)=v^\top M_{t,\ell}v\) for \(v\in L\).

definitions.name: Constrained-Gaussian face projection and post quadratic
definitions.construction: Compute \(V_h=\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in D_h}(v^\top Hv-2v^\top g)\) and then \(A_t(V_h)=V_h^\top M_tV_h\).

definitions.name: Finite conditional Gaussian face--knot experiment
definitions.construction: Condition on \(\mathscr S_\eta=\sigma(\eta)\). For \(\theta\in\Gamma_\eta\), draw \((g,Z)\sim N(0,\Sigma_\eta)\) with independent pre and post blocks, form \(\mathsf X_{\eta,\theta}\) from the shifted pre coordinate and shared-noise knot-group coordinates, and denote its conditional law by \(\Pr_{\eta,\theta}\). The statistic \(\eta\) contains every within-cell offset difference exactly; \(\theta\) contains only cross-cell group translations and simplex-face offsets.

definitions.name: Tail-box compactification of the conditional nuisance region
definitions.construction: On \(\mathcal B_{G,R}\), enumerate endpoint orders and active simplex faces, replace every face offset larger than \(2G/\lambda\) by that cap, preserve each known within-cell offset pattern, and cap successive shared-noise-group translation gaps at \(2R+2K_\eta\); the resulting finite union is \(\Gamma_\eta^{G,R}\).

definitions.name: Least common deterministic conditional cutoff
definitions.construction: For the admissible class \(\mathscr C_\eta\), set \(c^*(\eta,\alpha)=\inf\{c(\eta)\in\mathscr C_\eta:\inf_{\theta\in\Gamma_\eta}\Pr_{\eta,\theta}(\mathcal L_{\eta,\theta}\leq c(\eta))\geq1-\alpha\}\).

definitions.name: Two-donor, two-atom face-plus-collision certification instance
definitions.construction: Use the common outcome interval \([0,2]\), so \(D=2\), and set \(J=2\), \(S=2\), \(T_0=T_1=1\), \(f_{\min}=1/2\), \(f_{\max}=2\), and \(L_f=4\). In the pre period let \(Q_{1,1,\ell}(u)=u\), \(Q_{2,1,\ell}(u)=u+\tfrac25u(1-u)\), \(w_\ell=(1-h_f/\sqrt{n_\ell},h_f/\sqrt{n_\ell})\), and \(Q^N_{0,1,\ell}=w_{\ell1}Q_{1,1,\ell}+w_{\ell2}Q_{2,1,\ell}\). In the post period let donor one put mass \(1/2+h_c/\sqrt{m_\ell}\) at \(0\) and the remaining mass at \(1\), let donor two put masses \(1/2\) at \(0\) and \(2\), let the treated intervention law put masses \(1/2\) at \(0\) and \(1\), and define the no-intervention counterfactual by \(Q^N_{0,2,\ell}=w_{\ell1}Q_{1,2,\ell}+w_{\ell2}Q_{2,2,\ell}\). Each treated and donor pre cell has \(n_\ell\) independent observations, and each observed treated or donor post cell has \(m_\ell\) independent observations. Take \(0\leq h_f\leq\sqrt{n_\ell}\), \(0\leq h_c\leq\sqrt{m_\ell}/2\), and \(0<\lambda\leq1/375\). These clauses fix the triangular array and its induced local experiment \(\mathfrak E_{2,2}(h_f,h_c)\).

definitions.name: Finite-sample DKW fallback radius
definitions.construction: Using equal pre and post allocations of the error budget, set \(\varepsilon_{n,\ell}=\sqrt{\log(4(J+1)T_0/\alpha)/(2n_\ell)}\), \(\varepsilon_{m,\ell}=\sqrt{\log(4(J+1)T_1/\alpha)/(2m_\ell)}\), compute \(R_{w,\ell}\) as declared, and set \(R^{\mathrm{DKW}}_\ell=\min\{2D,2D\sqrt{\varepsilon_{m,\ell}}+D\sqrt J R_{w,\ell}\}\).

definitions.name: Certified nuisance-region and clustering handle
definitions.construction: Start from \(\mathsf{Handle}_{\mathrm{cert}}\): build simultaneous primitive confidence regions, enumerate support clusters and simplex faces consistent with them, retain exactly observed within-cell offsets, compactify unresolved translations and face offsets through \(\Gamma_\eta^{G,R}\), enclose Gaussian probabilities by deterministic interval arithmetic, spend an explicit tail and nuisance-exclusion budget, and return the rate-preserving DKW fallback if certification exceeds a deterministic work budget.

statements.statement: For every finite signed endpoint list satisfying \(\sum_qb_{tq,\ell}=0\), \(\|\sum_qb_{tq,\ell}\mathbf 1\{u>s_{tq,\ell}\}\|_{L^2}^2=-\tfrac12\sum_{q,q'}b_{tq,\ell}b_{tq',\ell}|s_{tq,\ell}-s_{tq',\ell}|\). Consequently the post-cell component satisfies the exact finite-array identity \(\|D_{t,\ell}^{\mathrm{post}}\|_{L^2}^2=m_\ell^{-1/2}\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}\). The energy is zero if and only if the coefficient sum at every distinct realized endpoint is zero, and \(|\Psi(s)-\Psi(s')|\leq(\sum_q|b_q|)^2\max_q|s_q-s'_q|\).
statements.justification: This exact identity keeps empirical and population endpoints separately anchored and supplies separation-free continuity before any local limit is introduced.
statements.gap: Gunsilius's Proposition~5 is the closest published discrete goodness-of-fit result, but the version-of-record equation was not accessible for formula-level verification and no verified statement there supplies this finite-sample independently anchored identity.
statements.consumer: It gives the exact unsmoothed error functional for the donor-identified post-treatment no-intervention quantile law needed in the mosquito-abundance QTE analysis of Zhai et al.

statements.statement: For every post period \(t\in\{T_0+1,\ldots,T_0+T_1\}\), the exact stable-span definitions have the following reductions. If \(\widehat w_\ell=w_\ell\), then \(E_{t,\ell}=m_\ell^{-1/2}\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}\). If the treated intervention law \(F^I_{0t,\ell}\) and every donor law \(F_{jt,\ell}\), \(1\leq j\leq J\), are point masses, then \(\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}=0\) and \(E_{t,\ell}=A_{t,\ell}(\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell)=n_\ell^{-1}A_{t,\ell}(\sqrt{n_\ell}(\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell))\). Thus known weights leave only the finite-support empirical-quantile error, point-mass post laws leave only the learned-weight quadratic, and imposing both conditions makes \(E_{t,\ell}=0\).
statements.justification: These two exact reductions audit that the endpoint and weight components correspond to the intended post-treatment counterfactual estimand.
statements.gap: The reductions are internal coherence checks rather than separate novelty claims; they connect the compound expansion to the fixed-weight discrete law and the standard tangent-cone quadratic special cases.
statements.consumer: They give referees and the Zhai et al. reanalysis immediate falsification checks for implementations with known weights or degenerate post cells.

statements.statement: From every subsequence of an array in \(\mathcal M\), one can extract a further subsequence such that, for the finitely many post knots, every scaled difference \(\sqrt{m_\ell}(c_{jtr,\ell}-c_{j'tr',\ell})\) converges in \(\overline{\mathbb R}\); the finite limits define within-cluster offsets \(d\), while absolute divergence defines distinct macro clusters. Along the same extraction, every \(\sqrt{n_\ell}w_{\ell j}\) converges in \([0,\infty]\) to \(h_j\), \(\rho_\ell\) converges in \([0,\infty]\), \(H_\ell\to H\), \(q_{t,\ell}\to q_t\) in \(L^2([0,1])^J\), \(M_{t,\ell}\to M_t\) for every post period, and the bounded jump and covariance coordinates admit joint limits. The maintained inequality for \(H_\ell\) passes to \(v^\top Hv\geq\lambda\|v\|_2^2\) on \(L\). This is a finite diagonal compactification, not a maintained local-alternative condition.
statements.justification: The extraction turns all finite-or-diverging knot gaps and face distances into theorem-local coordinates and creates the limit Gram \(H\) from the maintained finite-array Grams \(H_\ell\), without narrowing the primitive model.
statements.gap: Fang and Santos study fixed directionally differentiable maps; the compactification here is a finite diagonal argument specific to moving atomic knots and simplex faces, not an assumption borrowed from that paper.
statements.consumer: It guarantees that every potentially nonconvergent sampling allocation has phase-law limit points that can be audited.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathcal M\), \(\|\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell\|_2=O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2})\), with curvature supplied by \(v^\top H_\ell v\geq\lambda\|v\|_2^2\) on \(L\) at every \(\ell\). Along every extracted subsequence for which \(H_\ell\to H\) and \(\sqrt{n_\ell}w_{\ell j}\to h_j\in[0,\infty]\), \(\sqrt{n_\ell}(\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell)\Rightarrow V_h\), where only the subsequential limit criterion defining \(V_h\) uses \(H\). Moreover, \(A_t(V_h)=0\) almost surely if and only if all donor post-period quantile functions coincide almost everywhere; a projection face contributes an atom at zero exactly when that face lies in \(\ker M_t\).
statements.justification: Finite-array curvature identifies the weight uniformly, while its subsequential limit \(H\) governs the moving tangent-set Gaussian projection when the unique DSC weight approaches a simplex face.
statements.gap: Canen and Song give inference for a simplex-valued optimizer and Andrews gives boundary extremum limits; neither transports the projected score through a discrete post-period quantile loss.
statements.consumer: It identifies when learned boundary weights contribute first-order uncertainty to each post-period QTE curve relative to the donor-identified no-intervention counterfactual.

statements.statement: Set \(v_\ell=\sqrt{n_\ell}(\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell)\), \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}=(\widehat Q_{1t,\ell}-Q_{1t,\ell},\ldots,\widehat Q_{Jt,\ell}-Q_{Jt,\ell})^\top\), \(D_{t,\ell}=D^{\mathrm{post}}_{t,\ell}\), and \(B_{t,\ell}=\sqrt{m_\ell}\int_0^1q_{t,\ell}(u)D_{t,\ell}(u)du\). For every finite array and every \(t>T_0\), the exact decomposition is \(E_{t,\ell}=m_\ell^{-1/2}\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}+n_\ell^{-1}A_{t,\ell}(v_\ell)-2(n_\ell m_\ell)^{-1/2}v_\ell^\top B_{t,\ell}+n_\ell^{-1}\|v_\ell^\top\epsilon_{t,\ell}\|_{L^2}^2-2n_\ell^{-1/2}\langle D_{t,\ell},v_\ell^\top\epsilon_{t,\ell}\rangle+2n_\ell^{-1}\langle v_\ell^\top q_{t,\ell},v_\ell^\top\epsilon_{t,\ell}\rangle\). Uniformly over \(\mathcal M\) and jointly over post periods, each empirical quantile error is a bounded-height finite union of pulses whose total length is \(O_{\Pr}(m_\ell^{-1/2})\); therefore \(\|D_{t,\ell}\|_{L^1}=O_{\Pr}(m_\ell^{-1/2})\), \(B_{t,\ell}=O_{\Pr}(1)\), the displayed pre-weight--post-quantile cross term is \(O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2}m_\ell^{-1/2})\), and the last three terms are respectively \(O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1}m_\ell^{-1/2})\), \(O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2}m_\ell^{-1/2})\), and \(O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1}m_\ell^{-1/2})\). Hence \(r_{t,\ell}\) is their exact sum and \(\max_{t>T_0}|r_{t,\ell}|=O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2}m_\ell^{-1/2}+n_\ell^{-1}m_\ell^{-1/2})=o_{\Pr}(a_\ell)\). No subsequential coordinate occurs in this finite-array identity.
statements.justification: This exact algebra exposes every generated-weight term and uses finite-support pulse length to sharpen the pre-weight--post-quantile cross term to the order needed for all three phase laws.
statements.gap: Chen's residual-matching DSC and Alvarez--Orestes's continuous-cell DSC inference do not derive a finite-support endpoint expansion with an estimated fixed-donor simplex weight; no formula-level comparison to Gunsilius Proposition~5 is asserted without verified version-of-record text.
statements.consumer: It lets a study planner determine how pre-cell and post-cell replication control error in the identified post-treatment no-intervention quantile law.

statements.statement: Along every subsequence extracted by \(\mathrm{lem:local-subsequence-extraction}\), \(H_\ell\to H\), and there is one coupling carrying deterministic local objects \(d\), \(h\), and \(H\), together with all components of one jointly Gaussian vector \((g,Z)\) whose pre and post blocks are independent. On this coupling, jointly over post periods, \(v_\ell\to V_h\), \(A_{t,\ell}(v_\ell)\to A_t(V_h)\), \(\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}\to\Psi_t(d,Z)\), and \(B_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow B_t(d,Z)\). The pre-weight--post-quantile cross contribution obeys \(\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell}[-2(n_\ell m_\ell)^{-1/2}v_\ell^\top B_{t,\ell}]\Rightarrow-2V_h^\top B_t(d,Z)\), but it vanishes at every headline loss scale: multiplication by \(\sqrt{m_\ell}\) gives coefficient \(n_\ell^{-1/2}\) when \(\rho_\ell\to\infty\) or \(\rho_\ell\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)\), multiplication by \(n_\ell\) gives coefficient \(\sqrt{n_\ell/m_\ell}\) when \(\rho_\ell\to0\), and division by \(a_\ell\) gives coefficient \(\sqrt{n_\ell}/(n_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell})\to0\). The three remaining \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}\) terms vanish on the same scales. Consequently, whenever \(\omega=\lim n_\ell/(n_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell})\), \(E_{t,\ell}/a_\ell\Rightarrow(1-\omega)A_t(V_h)+\omega\Psi_t(d,Z)\). Equivalently, if \(\rho_\ell\to\infty\), then \(\sqrt{m_\ell}E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow\Psi_t(d,Z)\); if \(\rho_\ell\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)\), then \(\sqrt{m_\ell}E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow\Psi_t(d,Z)+A_t(V_h)/\kappa\); and if \(\rho_\ell\to0\), then \(n_\ell E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow A_t(V_h)\). The endpoint component is zero almost surely if and only if each almost-sure affine-endpoint equality class has coefficient sum zero, while the quadratic component is zero almost surely if and only if all donor post quantile functions coincide almost everywhere.
statements.justification: The common coupling includes the face projection, anchored endpoint energy, and sharp cross-vector limit, showing that the nonzero cross effect is visible only at its own finer scale and cannot alter the normalized loss or any phase law.
statements.gap: The direct DSC comparators Chen and Alvarez--Orestes do not supply the exact quantile-span atomic-endpoint and local simplex-face experiment. Gunsilius supplies the model and a discrete goodness-of-fit theorem, but the inaccessible version-of-record equation is not used for a formula-level tightening claim.
statements.consumer: It determines which sampling source controls precision for the donor-identified post-treatment no-intervention law when the Zhai et al. abundance design allocates observations between pre fitting and post cells.

statements.statement: The DKW construction yields \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}\Pr_P\{(\tau_{t,\ell})_{t>T_0}\in\mathcal C_\ell(R^{\mathrm{DKW}}_\ell)\}\geq1-\alpha\) for every \(n_\ell,m_\ell\), and \(R^{\mathrm{DKW}}_\ell=O(n_\ell^{-1/2}+m_\ell^{-1/4})\) uniformly. For \(\alpha<1/2\), two legal smooth-pre and Bernoulli-post subexperiments imply that no uniformly honest ball has worst-case diameter \(o(n_\ell^{-1/2}+m_\ell^{-1/4})\).
statements.justification: This supplies an always-valid fallback whose shrinking order is not sacrificed when sharp calibration cannot be certified.
statements.gap: Chernozhukov et al. invert simultaneous CDF bands into pointwise-in-quantile envelopes; they do not give the learned-weight simultaneous \(L^2\) radius or its two-sample minimax order.
statements.consumer: The result gives a defensible simultaneous uncertainty summary for the complete post-period abundance-QTE path relative to the donor-identified no-intervention counterfactual.

statements.statement: In the one-donor equal-Bernoulli post subexperiment with donor knot displacement \(h_B/\sqrt{m_\ell}\), the simplex is the singleton \(\Delta_1=\{1\}\), so \(\widehat w_\ell=w_\ell=1\), \(v_\ell=0\), and the weight quadratic, \(B_{t,\ell}\) cross contribution, and all \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}\) remainder terms are identically zero. The anchored limit is \(\Psi^B_{h_B}=|Z_0-h_B-Z_1|+|Z_0|+|Z_1|-|Z_0-h_B|-|h_B+Z_1|+h_B\), where \(Z_0,Z_1\) are independent \(N(0,1/4)\). Its exact distribution function reduces to a one-dimensional Gaussian integral, and the least common 95 percent squared-radius cutoff \(c_B^*\) satisfies \(1.913<c_B^*\leq1.914\), while the collision-oracle cutoff is \(1.38590382435\). Any uniformly honest plug-in-centered radius with a deterministic collision limit has that limit at least \(c_B^*\).
statements.justification: The explicit frontier proves that uniform local honesty costs strictly more than collision-oracle calibration.
statements.gap: Robins--van der Vaart and Hoffmann--Nickl give general adaptation obstructions, but neither computes the least-favorable intermediate knot offset for this discrete DSC QTE loss.
statements.consumer: It prevents collision-only or separated-only critical values from undercovering the post-treatment intervention-versus-no-intervention QTE at nearly colliding mosquito-abundance masses.

statements.statement: In the finite experiment \(\{\Pr_{\eta,\theta}:\theta\in\Gamma_\eta\}\) conditional on \(\mathscr S_\eta\), \(c^*(\eta,\alpha)=\sup_{\theta\in\Gamma_\eta}Q_{1-\alpha}^{\Pr_{\eta,\theta}}(\mathcal L_{\eta,\theta})\). It is the least member of \(\mathscr C_\eta\) satisfying \(\inf_{\theta\in\Gamma_\eta}\Pr_{\eta,\theta}\{\mathcal L_{\eta,\theta}\leq c(\eta)\}\geq1-\alpha\); no optimality over randomized or observation-dependent radii is claimed. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), choose \(G\) and \(R\) with certified Gaussian tail probability at most \(\varepsilon/8\). On \(\mathcal B_{G,R}\), replacing \(\Gamma_\eta\) by \(\Gamma_\eta^{G,R}\) preserves the loss, and finite active-set enumeration, interval enclosures for Gaussian rectangle probabilities, grid refinement, and bisection terminate with deterministic brackets for both the worst-case coverage probability and \(c^*(\eta,\alpha)\) of width at most \(\varepsilon\), including structural-zero cases.
statements.justification: The theorem gives the exact decision meaning and a terminating certified calculation for the honest local common-cutoff frontier.
statements.gap: Andrews--Mikusheva conditional inference and Cox--Shi active-rank testing inform the construction, but neither computes a deterministic common cutoff for a cone-projection plus signed-endpoint loss.
statements.consumer: It supplies a finite, auditable oracle benchmark for feasible calibration of the abundance QTE relative to the donor-identified no-intervention law.

statements.statement: The array in \(\mathrm{def:j2s2-instance}\), with common interval \([0,2]\) and \(D=2\), belongs to \(\mathcal M\): its pre laws meet the smooth-density bounds, its same weight spans both pre and post no-intervention quantiles, its observed post laws have at most two atoms, and its pooled Gram satisfies the maintained bound for \(0<\lambda\leq1/375\). For every \(\kappa\in(0,\infty)\), \(G,R>0\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), the compactification and interval algorithm of \(\mathrm{thm:oracle-common-cutoff}\) terminates for the certified family \(\{\mathfrak E_{2,2}(h_f,h_c):0\leq h_f\leq2G/\lambda,\ 0\leq h_c\leq2R\}\). It returns an interval of width at most \(\varepsilon\) containing \(\sup_{0\leq h_f\leq2G/\lambda,\,0\leq h_c\leq2R}Q_{0.95}\{(1+\kappa)^{-1}A_t(V_{(\infty,h_f)})+\kappa(1+\kappa)^{-1}\Psi_t(h_c,Z)\}\), and every coverage probability used in the optimization is enclosed between explicit lower and upper Gaussian-cell sums differing by at most \(\varepsilon\). As \(R\to\infty\) and then \(\kappa\to\infty\), the face term vanishes and the certified family reduces to the one-donor Bernoulli problem, where \(\widehat w_\ell=w_\ell=1\) and every weight and cross term is zero, reproducing \(1.913<c_B^*\leq1.914\).
statements.justification: This finite face-plus-collision instance is the early kill test for the claimed certification machinery and links it to the independently checked Bernoulli bracket.
statements.gap: No direct DSC inference paper supplies a certified probability enclosure for a simultaneous local simplex face and atomic knot collision.
statements.consumer: It gives a reproducible validation case before calibration of the intervention-versus-no-intervention QTE is applied to higher-dimensional mosquito-abundance support patterns.

statements.statement: Can one construct from \(\mathsf{Handle}_{\mathrm{cert}}\) a measurable radius \(R_\ell\) such that \(\mathcal C_\ell(R_\ell)\) has asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M\), has diameter \(O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2}+m_\ell^{-1/4})\), uses the DKW branch with probability \(o(1)\) on every supported fixed local stratum, satisfies \(R_\ell^2/a_\ell\to c^*(\eta,\alpha)\) conditionally on \(\mathscr S_\eta\), learns within-cell offsets exactly at the local limit while retaining cross-cell translations and face offsets in the nuisance region, and reduces only on fixed separated interior strata with continuous nondegenerate critical law to the corresponding oracle cutoff?
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing open content: one total procedure must remain honest through support, covariance-rank, and simplex-face changes while attaining the conditional deterministic-cutoff frontier.
statements.gap: Chen supplies residual-matching DSC and Alvarez--Orestes supplies continuous-cell quantile-mixture inference, but no located result combines exact quantile-span DSC, atomic endpoint conditioning, estimated face weights, nuisance exclusion budgeting, and certified common-cutoff attainment.
statements.consumer: A successful construction permits an unsmoothed simultaneous \(L^2\) reanalysis of the Zhai et al. mosquito-abundance QTE curves relative to the donor-identified post-treatment no-intervention law, while excluding their separate binary elimination estimand.

sampling_model.design: Fixed \(J\), \(T_0\), and \(T_1\) repeated-cross-section distributional synthetic-control panel in which one simplex weight \(w_\ell\) spans the treated no-intervention quantile law in every pre-treatment and post-treatment panel period.
sampling_model.units: The treated and donor cell laws are fixed primitives; each pre cell contributes \(n_\ell\) independent draws and each post cell contributes \(m_\ell\) independent draws.
sampling_model.treatment: Only unit \(j=0\) is intervened upon after period \(T_0\); donor post laws and \(F^I_{0t,\ell}\) are observed, while \(F^N_{0t,\ell}\) is the post-treatment no-intervention counterfactual identified by the same \(w_\ell\) learned from pre-treatment periods.
sampling_model.overlap: No atom-mass lower bound, post-knot separation, interior-weight restriction, or restriction on \(n_\ell/m_\ell\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Pre quantiles, the simplex weight, the finite-array Gram \(H_\ell\), score covariance, post multinomial masses, support clusters, and within-cell offset differences are estimated with simultaneous confidence regions; within-cell differences become exactly observed coordinates in the local experiment, while cross-cell translations and face offsets remain in a certified nuisance region with a rate-preserving fallback. The matrix \(H\) appears only after local-subsequence extraction as a limit of \(H_\ell\).

estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_{t,\ell}=\widehat Q^I_{0t,\ell}-\sum_{j=1}^J\widehat w_{\ell j}\widehat Q_{jt,\ell}\), with \(Q^N_{0t,\ell}=\sum_{j=1}^Jw_{\ell j}Q_{jt,\ell}\), exact finite-array loss \(m_\ell^{-1/2}\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}+n_\ell^{-1}A_{t,\ell}(v_\ell)-2(n_\ell m_\ell)^{-1/2}v_\ell^\top B_{t,\ell}\) plus the three displayed \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}\) terms, and conditional squared-radius calibration \(a_\ell c^*(\eta,\alpha)\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section~5.3.2 and Proposition~5 provide a published discrete distributional-synthetic-control goodness-of-fit limit; its version-of-record formula was not accessible for a finer claim.

The version-of-record Summary states that counterfactuals are identified by matching treated pre-intervention quantile residuals to a convex combination of control residuals orthogonal to observable common factors.
Section~6.2, Assumptions~4--6, and Corollary~3 give DSC inference for smooth continuous empirical quantiles with a donor-dilution condition.
Theorem~2 gives a convergence rate for DSC weights under interior-weight and quantile-draw conditions.
Theorem~2 transforms simultaneous distribution-function bands into valid bands for discrete quantile functions.
The main theorem gives an asymptotically uniformly valid confidence set for a simplex-valued optimizer weight.
Theorem~1 gives uniformly asymptotically valid conditional critical values with a functional nuisance parameter.
Theorem~1 gives finite-sample validity and size exactness for active-rank Gaussian moment-inequality testing.

tldr: Exact discrete distributional synthetic control identifies the treated unit's no-intervention quantile law in every pre-treatment and post-treatment panel period with one stable simplex weight. Its QTE estimator has two first-order error sources on different scales: an exact finite-array signed endpoint energy from empirical post-period atoms and a cone-projected quadratic from simplex weight estimation. The exact squared-error decomposition also retains the pre-weight--post-quantile cross term and three donor-quantile remainder terms. Finite-support pulse geometry makes the cross term \(O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2}m_\ell^{-1/2})\): it has the joint limit \(-2V_h^\top B_t(d,Z)\) at its own \(\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell}\) scale but vanishes in the normalized loss and all three \(n_\ell/\sqrt{m_\ell}\) phase laws. Uniform identification is imposed on the finite-array Grams \(H_\ell\), while \(H\) appears only as their local-subsequence limit. The project also proves rate-optimal uniformly honest simultaneous \(L^2\) QTE balls and defines the least common deterministic conditional cutoff in a fully specified finite Gaussian experiment. A legal \(J=2\), \(S=2\), \(D=2\) face-plus-collision calculation reduces in its post-dominated restriction to the one-donor Bernoulli 95 percent honesty bracket \((1.913,1.914]\), versus the collision-oracle value \(1.38590382435\); all weight and cross terms vanish in that restriction. The open theorem is a measurable support-cluster and nuisance-region procedure that attains this cutoff while remaining uniformly honest through changing supports, covariance ranks, and simplex faces, with oracle calibration only on separated regular strata.

project_justification.gap: Chen's published DSC identifies counterfactuals by pre-intervention quantile-residual matching, Gunsilius supplies the quantile-span model and discrete goodness-of-fit asymptotics, and Alvarez--Orestes gives direct DSC inference under smooth continuous-cell and donor-dilution conditions. None supplies inference for a post-treatment no-intervention quantile law identified by an exact period-stable span together with the exact atomic-endpoint and local simplex-face experiment, the pulse-sharp generated-weight cross-vector calculation, its three two-sample phases, or a uniformly honest certified common cutoff; no formula-level claim about Gunsilius Proposition~5 is used because its version-of-record equation was inaccessible.
project_justification.niche: Fixed donors, independent pre and post cell samples, one exact span weight across all pre-treatment and post-treatment no-intervention laws, and exact finite-support post laws generate a two-scale experiment. The squared error contains endpoint and face-leading terms plus a pre-weight--post-quantile cross term that is nonzero at its own finer scale but vanishes under every headline normalization. Within-cell mass offsets are asymptotically observed exactly, whereas cross-cell knot translations and local face offsets remain nuisance parameters. Uniform identification is a finite-array condition on \(H_\ell\), while finite diagonal extraction compactifies all scaled gaps and defines \(H\) only as a local-subsequence limit without imposing a new local-array assumption.
project_justification.fill: The theorem program combines the exact six-term finite-array squared-error decomposition, a sharp pulse-geometry bound and joint limit for the pre-weight--post-quantile cross vector, finite-array Gram curvature, the normalized compound loss and three phase laws, exact known-weight and point-mass reductions, the Bernoulli honesty penalty, deterministic conditional-cutoff experiment, legal \(J=2\), \(S=2\), \(D=2\) certificate, and DKW fallback around one falsifiable open target: feasible cutoff attainment with exclusion-budgeted conditional regions and a rate-preserving fallback.

related_work: Chen's Journal of Applied Econometrics article is a direct DSC comparator: its version-of-record Summary on p.~505 identifies counterfactuals by matching a vector of treated pre-intervention quantile residuals to a convex combination of control residuals, with residuals orthogonal to observable common factors for poor matching. That residual-factor construction does not state the exact common-weight equality for the treated no-intervention quantile law in every pre-treatment and post-treatment panel period, and it does not supply an atomic-endpoint/simplex-face local experiment or the generated-weight cross-vector limit. Gunsilius establishes the Wasserstein-quantile DSC model for arbitrary one-dimensional outcome laws and gives a discrete goodness-of-fit result in Proposition~5 and Appendix~A.6. The version-of-record full equation was inaccessible in this source check, so the proposal treats Gunsilius as the model and discrete-asymptotic anchor without asserting that its published formula pools knot noise or omits a particular cross term. Alvarez and Orestes are the other direct DSC inference comparator: Section~6.2, Assumptions~4--6, and Corollary~3 treat smooth continuous empirical quantiles with ridge regularization and a donor-dilution condition, not fixed-donor atomic post cells with local collisions, faces, and pulse-sharp cross-term control. Zhang, Zhang, and Zhang study DSC prediction and weight rates under quantile-grid and interior-weight conditions, which informs but does not settle the present cell-sampling experiment with finite-array curvature \(H_\ell\) and local-subsequence limit \(H\). Sommerfeld and Munk derive directional limits for empirical finite-space Wasserstein distances, supplying the atomic-transport precedent without a generated DSC barycenter. Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val, Melly, and Wuthrich project simultaneous distribution-function bands into honest discrete quantile and quantile-effect bands; the DKW fallback uses that coverage logic but targets a learned-weight simultaneous \(L^2\) ball. Andrews supplies tangent-cone extremum asymptotics, and Canen and Song supply uniformly valid simplex-weight inference; neither composes the face projection, endpoint energy, and vanishing cross vector. Andrews and Mikusheva condition on Gaussian nuisance statistics, while Cox and Shi enumerate active constraints; these techniques inform the conditional experiment and certification but do not give its compound-loss cutoff. Robins and van der Vaart and Hoffmann and Nickl establish general honesty-versus-adaptation obstructions; the Bernoulli theorem computes the exact penalty for this collision experiment. Zhai et al. are the same-question consumer: their abundance analysis smooths discrete quantiles and reports pointwise percentile-bootstrap intervals, whereas this project targets the raw discrete post-treatment contrast between the observed intervention law and the donor-identified no-intervention law with simultaneous \(L^2\) coverage; their separate binary CDF and \(W_1\) elimination analysis is outside scope.
technical_internal_limitation: The local criterion minimizes only the common deterministic conditional squared-radius cutoff over \(\mathscr C_\eta\); it does not optimize expected radius, randomized rules, or arbitrary observation-dependent radius rules. The finite Gaussian object is a conditional loss experiment, not an unrestricted deficiency equivalence for the raw samples. The general oracle calculation uses the normalized leading loss \((1-\omega)A_t(V_h)+\omega\Psi_t(d,Z)\); the sharper cross term is nondegenerate only at its own finer scale and therefore does not alter that cutoff algorithm. The calculation retains exactly observed within-cell offsets and treats cross-cell translations and face offsets as nuisance. The DKW ball proves honest rate attainment, while feasible sharp conditional calibration remains open. Applying the result to Zhai et al. would additionally require a bridge for discrete pre-period outcomes, beta-weighted quantile fitting, period aggregation, spatial dependence, and interpolation.
honest_scope: The exact endpoint identity, exact six-term finite-array squared-error decomposition, pulse-sharp bound and joint local limit for \(B_{t,\ell}\), diagonal local compactification with \(H_\ell\to H\), normalized compound loss, coupled three-phase limits, component degeneracy criteria, exact known-weight and point-mass reductions, DKW upper rate, matching worst-case rate lower bound, Bernoulli honesty penalty, deterministic oracle cutoff, and legal \(J=2\), \(S=2\), \(D=2\) certificate are theorem targets. The cross contribution can be nondegenerate at its own \(\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell}\) scale but vanishes from every headline loss normalization. The stable-span model identifies \(Q^N_{0t,\ell}\) with the same \(w_\ell\) for every pre-treatment period and every post-treatment no-intervention period; it never equates that counterfactual law with \(Q^I_{0t,\ell}\). Feasible attainment of the conditional cutoff across changing support, covariance rank, and simplex face is explicitly open. Within-cell local offsets are conditioned on as exactly observed coordinates; cross-cell translations and face offsets remain nuisance. Oracle calibration is claimed only on fixed separated interior strata with continuous nondegenerate critical laws. If all relevant post laws are point masses, \(\Psi_t=0\) and the limit reduces to the standard tangent-cone quadratic; with known weights, the quadratic and every generated-weight cross or remainder term vanish and the result reduces to a finite-support empirical quantile law. In the one-donor Bernoulli restriction, \(\widehat w_\ell=w_\ell=1\), so all weight and cross terms are identically zero.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Construct a measurable certified nuisance-region and support/face clustering procedure that is uniformly honest and conditionally minimax.
seed_details.summary: Combine separately anchored endpoint loss with simplex-cone projection, condition on exactly observed within-cell offsets, and certify the least common cutoff over the remaining local nuisance region.
seed_details.anchor_read: The anchor's Introduction and Methods motivate distributional abundance effects, smooth discrete trap counts by interpolation, fit pooled quantile weights, and report 500-replication pointwise percentile intervals; its Discussion and Conclusion interpret heterogeneous suppression but acknowledge aggregation and interference limitations.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace smoothed pointwise bootstrap quantiles by a total Borel partition built from empirical CDF, support, Gram, and face information, retaining rather than selecting away unresolved knot translations and boundary offsets.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing discrete DSC, simplex-face inference, support collisions, and certified conditional cutoffs found no paper combining all four; the closest components are Chernozhukov et al., Canen--Song, and Andrews--Mikusheva.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from conditioning plus active-rank chi-square calibration because every nuisance coordinate is either observed or projected out.
seed_details.rebuttal: The endpoint energy is not chi-square, its law changes at intermediate knot offsets, within-cell and cross-cell offsets have different observability, and support clustering errors can change both anchors and cone dimension.

seed_details.summary: Prove a uniform two-source expansion with separately anchored endpoint energy, a constrained-Gaussian quadratic, cross-term control, and if-and-only-if degeneracy criteria.
seed_details.anchor_read: Sections~3.2 and~5.3.2, Proposition~5, and Appendix~A.6 of the public manuscript provide the model and discrete-asymptotic anchor; the version-of-record formula was inaccessible, so no claim that it pools knot noise is used.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Retain every empirical and population cumulative-mass endpoint separately in the finite-array loss and expand the estimated weight at its tangent-cone scale before taking a common local-subsequence limit.
seed_details.destination_search: Sommerfeld--Munk occupy fixed-law finite-space transport limits and Andrews occupies boundary extremum limits, but no located theorem composes them for learned fixed-donor DSC or produces the three two-sample phases.

seed_details.rebuttal: Their sum does not determine the separately anchored one-dimensional energy, the shared post-period weight source, the cross term, the phase normalization, or exact component degeneracy.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Characterize the sharp penalty for honesty over locally indistinguishable collision and face strata.
seed_details.summary: Give a contiguous-alternative lower bound and a separated-stratum upper procedure, with exact local cutoff loss rather than a qualitative impossibility.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction frames honest Hilbert confidence sets through testing rates, the main construction estimates squared loss on a split sample, and the concluding discussion separates adaptive centers from unavoidable diameter enlargement.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace smoothness-class testing alternatives by coupled finite-support mass, knot, and simplex-face perturbations at the two local sample scales.
seed_details.destination_search: Hoffmann--Nickl provides separation-based necessity and sufficiency for smoothness bands, but searches found no two-scale collision/face separation frontier for DSC QTE balls.
seed_details.red_team: The general testing-modulus theory already implies the claimed nonadaptation.
seed_details.rebuttal: It implies a template, not the exact compound local experiment, the observable separation coordinates, the phase-specific boundary, or the numerical honesty constant.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Certify the least stable common cutoff in the one-donor Bernoulli local-collision experiment.

seed_details.anchor_read: Gunsilius provides the published discrete DSC goodness-of-fit anchor; the separately sampled Bernoulli calculation is positioned as a new explicit local honesty frontier without a formula-level allegation about the inaccessible version-of-record display.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Rotate the two independent bridge errors into sum and difference coordinates before integrating the signed overlap length.
seed_details.destination_search: No located paper computes this DSC-specific cutoff; generic Gaussian confidence-set duality would subsume only the abstract minimax definition.

seed_details.rebuttal: The objection limits the seed to a sharp supporting theorem; it is retained only inside the broader certified-cutoff proposal.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Transfer the raw two-sample DSC experiment to the face--knot Gaussian loss experiment for discontinuous coverage and unbounded radius loss.
seed_details.summary: Establish local deficiency bounds or matching upper and lower risk-transfer lemmas on compact face and knot nuisance sets.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction treats weak identification as a functional nuisance problem, Theorem~1 adds an arbitrarily small critical-value inflation for possible atoms, and its proof uses uniform Gaussian approximation and Lipschitz control of conditional critical values.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Strengthen bounded-Lipschitz coupling to control confidence-event boundaries and uniform integrability after the nonsmooth endpoint and projection maps.
seed_details.destination_search: Uniform Gaussian approximation papers cover maxima and smooth empirical processes, but no located transfer result handles simultaneous support relabeling, singular bridge ranks, and moving simplex faces.
seed_details.red_team: The continuous mapping theorem and anti-concentration make transfer automatic.
seed_details.rebuttal: Coverage indicators are discontinuous, face projections can create atoms, and squared-radius risk is unbounded; each requires a separate uniform argument.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Convert simultaneous cellwise distribution-function bands into an honest learned-weight \(L^2\) QTE ball.

seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for a conservative rate result, so this seed is retained only as the fallback construction and not as the headline.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped as a headline because it would be a routine composition and would not attain the conditional local cutoff.

seed_details.summary: Numerically estimate the joint directional derivative and bootstrap the compound local loss.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction isolates directional but nonlinear derivatives, the main theorem characterizes ordinary-bootstrap validity, the derivative-aware resampling theorem repairs it, and the Conclusion stresses local size control.

seed_details.destination_search: Hong--Li already gives numerical directional differentiation for convex Lipschitz maps; without a certified nuisance supremum this route does not solve uniform honesty.
seed_details.red_team: Numerical directional bootstrap is already available for convex nonsmooth functionals.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection largely holds: support and face selection remain nonuniform, so this is a computational ingredient rather than an independent kernel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped because relabeling an existing derivative-aware bootstrap would not certify the changing nuisance region.

literature_map.subsumption_check: The direct DSC comparators occupy residual matching, model construction, continuous-cell inference, and interior weight-rate components. The unoccupied target is their nonregular composition under exact atomic post laws: a six-term finite-array squared-error identity, a pulse-sharp cross-vector limit that disappears only at the headline scales, a local face--collision experiment, and a certified honest deterministic common cutoff. Gunsilius is not assigned a formula-level comparator promise beyond the accessible source text.

novelty_justification.precise_gap: Chen supplies pre-intervention quantile-residual matching under observable-factor orthogonality, Gunsilius supplies the exact quantile-span model and discrete goodness-of-fit asymptotics, and Alvarez--Orestes supplies continuous-cell DSC inference with donor dilution. None states the fixed-donor atomic endpoint plus local simplex-face Gaussian experiment for a post-treatment no-intervention quantile law identified by the same span weight used in every pre-treatment period, the exact generated-weight cross term and its pulse-sharp order, its three two-sample phases, or the certified honest common cutoff.
novelty_justification.why_not_subsumed: The finite-array endpoint loss retains each empirical and population knot separately, the learned weight is identified by the finite-array Gram \(H_\ell\) and contributes at order \(n_\ell^{-1}\), and post atoms contribute at order \(m_\ell^{-1/2}\). The pre-weight--post-quantile interaction has a nonzero \(\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell}\)-scale limit but pulse geometry proves that it vanishes under every headline normalization. Only after local-subsequence extraction does \(H_\ell\to H\) enter the cone projection. Their composition creates three phase laws, exactly observed within-cell offset differences, unresolved cross-cell translations, and a compound non-chi-square cutoff problem absent from the direct comparators.
novelty_justification.chosen_kernel_reason: The certified procedure is the highest-value survivor because the presolved endpoint algebra, cone geometry, Bernoulli frontier, and finite compactification make it falsifiable while leaving a substantial measurable uniform-attainment theorem. It directly delivers the inferential object missing from the application.
novelty_justification.adversarial_boundary: At a one-donor Bernoulli collision, the 95 percent collision-oracle squared cutoff is \(1.38590382435\), but contiguous intermediate displacements force the least common cutoff above \(1.913\). Any claim of oracle adaptation without a statistically separated stratum therefore undercovers on an explicit legal subexperiment.
